title: INT8 GPTQ/AWQ verification bridge and calibration regression harness
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Purpose: build a reusable verification bridge that translates GPTQ/AWQ weight-only INT8 profile outputs into runtime-ready config and a regression harness that validates accuracy and stability across canary -> full rollout. This ticket covers the integration glue, calibration orchestration, automated acceptance tests, and a chaos/edge-case regression suite.

Scope: implement a converter from profile artifacts (calibration stats, per-tensor scale/zero info) to the runtime quantization config schema; calibration orchestration glue to run profile sweeps; CI job that runs smoke + nightly accuracy/regression; canary gating rules and metrics; telemetry exports for per-token logprob delta and semantic-sim similarity.

Non-goals: training changes to GPTQ/AWQ algorithms, new quant format (FP8), or UX changes in the Console dashboard beyond dashboard links for canary gating (separate PR).
background: We already have multiple INT8 weight-only CI tickets (calibration pipelines and regtests) but profiles from new GPTQ/AWQ toolchain produce a slightly different artifact layout and per-axis scale conventions. Without a small compatibility layer the runtime can't consume them and our existing regression harnesses miss edge cases introduced by AWQ's chunked scales. Customers are starting to test AWQ-quantized models and want predictable canary behavior.
goals: Create a profile->runtime config bridge compatible with both GPTQ and AWQ produced artifacts
Add a calibration orchestration step to the profile pipeline that emits validation traces and synthetic coverage snapshots
Implement automated CI jobs: quick smoke (pre-merge), nightly regression (full eval), and an OOB chaos run (failure injection) for memory/regression flakiness
Define canary gating thresholds and wire telemetry: median token logprob delta, 95th-percentile latency, semantic-similarity drop (embedding cosine), and fail/pass counters
out_of_scope: Rewriting the inference runtime quant kernels
FP8 profile support (handled by separate RFC)
Console UX redesign for rollout policy
design_decisions: Bridge will be implemented as a small library (python) installed in the profile pipeline and the runtime side loader will accept the unified JSON config

Use token-level log-prob delta + embedding cosine similarity over curated seed prompts as primary accuracy signals rather than aggregate perplexity (more sensitive to hallucination and downstream metrics)
Nightly regression will use a reservoir of 2k prompts with stratified buckets: long-form, instruction-following, code, and completion; smoke uses a 50-prompt focused shot set
Canary gating logic: fail if semantic-sim drop > 3% and median logprob delta > 0.8 nats OR if end-to-end task pass-rate delta > 2% on golden prompts
test_plan: Unit tests: converter mapping tests for tensor names and axis conventions (GPTQ vs AWQ examples)
Integration: deploy a canary on dedicated-staging with both GPTQ and AWQ variants and run the smoke prompt set; assert gates
Nightly E2E: run full evaluation suite, compare against golden baseline stored in s3://redwood-ci/quant-baselines/runtime-1.20/awq-gptq/
Chaos tests: scheduled GPU memory pressure and RPC error injection during calibration to verify graceful rollback and retry behavior
acceptance_criteria: Converter library accepts both GPTQ and AWQ profile artifacts and emits a runtime JSON with schema v2; unit coverage >= 85%
Canary job automatically fails a rollout if any gate breaches and posts a failure summary to #quant-alerts with links to diffs and logs
Nightly regression produces a drift report and stores metric deltas; alerts fire when semantic-sim or logprob thresholds cross configured values
Runbook updated: rollback steps, mitigation for mis-calibrated scales, and emergency flagging procedure included in the PRD and Confluence
steps: 1) Define unified runtime config schema (schema v2) for weight-only INT8 profiles and document field semantics
2) Implement converter in profile pipeline (python package) with CLI and library API
3) Add integration tests in runtime integration repo that load converted config and run perf/accuracy harness
4) Add CI jobs: pre-merge smoke (fast), nightly regression (full), and weekly chaos injection
5) Instrument telemetry exports in the runtime for logprob deltas and semantic-sim scores
6) Create canary gating rules in the Console config and wire automated rollback/notification
7) Run a staged rollout: internal -> dedicated-staging -> canary -> full rollout
8) Publish results and runbook, and schedule a postmortem after first full rollout

2026-02-12: Calibration orchestration added: automatic retrain of calibration stats with chunk overlap tuning; reduced median delta to 0.42 in staging. Logs: https://console.redwood.ai/logs/quant/1248
2026-02-20: Added telemetry counters and semantic-sim calculation; initial dashboard tiles created. Opening follow-up ticket for telemetry aggregation perf (ENG-71400).
2026-03-02: Canary policy drafted and reviewed by SRE and Product. Review notes: need explicit timeout on calibration runs to avoid blocking canary (addressed in PR #1248).

2026-03-08: Nightly regression job pipeline configured; first nightly completed with full 2k prompt suite. Drift report uploaded to s3 and linked in dashboard. Two prompts exceed tolerance; creating investigations (see comments).
notes: Reviewer feedback from Runtime: ensure converter maps AWQ chunked scales to contiguous runtime arrays — existing mapping code had an off-by-one in axis ordering
SRE request: keep canary window to 30 minutes with automatic fallback to previous model variant on any gate fail
Product: define customer-facing FAQ in case canaries block upgrades; coordinate with Solutions Engineering for early customers testing AWQ models
